# Tryll Engine (https://tryllengine.com)

> Tryll is on-device AI middleware for game engines (Unity, Unreal Engine 5 and proprietary engines). It gives in-game characters a realistic mind: they understand natural language, remember what the player did and act accordingly, running on the player's GPU with no servers, no per-token fees, and no user data leaving the device. Built by game developers; Epic MegaGrants recipient, funded by Early Game Ventures.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tryllengine.com/): what Tryll does, use cases, client stories, pricing, contact
- [For Developers](https://tryllengine.com/features): features for basic and advanced NPCs, developer tools, performance and memory
- [Get Tryll Engine](https://tryllengine.com/download): plugins for Unity 6+ and Unreal Engine 5.7+, system requirements, install guides
- [Demo game: Tryll Colony](https://tryllengine.com/demo): a short scene where you talk your way through and characters react in real time
- [About](https://tryllengine.com/about): founders and team
- [Blog](https://tryllengine.com/blog): engineering deep-dives, product updates and event news
- [Tryll Assistant](https://tryllengine.com/tryll-assistant): free on-device AI game guide overlay on Steam
- [Documentation](https://docs.tryllengine.com/): API reference, how-to guides, model benchmarks
- [Privacy Policy](https://tryllengine.com/privacy-policy)

## What Tryll does

- **Smart NPCs**: characters that understand natural language, remember what the player did, and act accordingly
- **Real Talk**: speech-to-text and text-to-speech on the player's device, with voiced NPCs in many languages (including Korean and Japanese) without recording every line
- **Dynamic worlds**: you set the world and its rules; Tryll creates agents and keeps them within those rules
- **New genres**: mechanics built on conversation that weren't possible before
- **Developer tools**: Dialog Tester, Agent Log, server memory inspector, dialog variant comparison, workflow graphs in the Unity and Unreal editors

## How to get started

1. Install the plugin; a Tryll tab appears in the editor
2. Download an open model into the project; Tryll runs it on the player's GPU
3. Build an agent: connect lore, define its role and allowed actions, test it in the Dialog Tester

## Pricing

- **Free** until a shipped game passes $500k USD in gross revenue; then a 1% royalty. No seats, no per-token fees.
- Free for game developers, individuals and small businesses under $500k, and for educators and schools with no revenue limit
- **Extra services** (custom pricing): forward-deployed engineering, QA and evals, security guardrails, custom AI components

## System requirements

- **Developers**: Windows 10/11 64-bit; Unity 6+ or Unreal Engine 5.7+; NVIDIA, AMD or Intel GPU (8 GB VRAM recommended for local testing); 16 GB RAM; 10–20 GB disk for models
- **Players**: any GPU with 8 GB VRAM or more, which covers about 3 in 4 Steam PCs (Steam Hardware Survey, 07/2026). One build serves a richer or leaner model per machine.
- **Platforms**: Windows PC today; console and mobile runtimes on the roadmap
